subject: math
title: Grade 2 Fractions and Fair Shares
seo_title: Grade 2 Fractions and Fair Shares Worksheets: Free Math Practice with Answer Key (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Use drawings to represent, solve, and compare the results of fair-share problems that involve sharing up to 10 items among 2, 3, 4, and 6 sharers, including problems that result in whole numbers, mixed numbers, and fractional amounts
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 math worksheets on fractions and fair shares for the Ontario curriculum: halves, thirds, fourths and sixths, sharing up to 10 items fairly, comparing shares and one third = two sixths. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Fair shares are equal shares. More sharers means smaller shares.
key_sub: 5 sandwiches shared by 2 friends: 2 each, then cut the last one in half. Each friend gets 2 and a half. One third is the same as two sixths.
body_html:
Equal parts

A fraction is part of a whole. The parts must be equal: all the same size.

2 equal parts are halves. 3 equal parts are thirds. 4 equal parts are fourths. 6 equal parts are sixths.

Equal partsNameOne part
2halvesone half
3thirdsone third
4fourthsone fourth
6sixthsone sixth

Fair shares

A fair share means everyone gets the same amount. Give the items out one at a time until none are left.

Sometimes items are left over. Cut each leftover item into as many equal pieces as there are friends.

Example

8 apples are shared by 4 friends.

Give them out one at a time. 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8.

Answer: 2 apples each

Example

7 oranges are shared by 3 friends.

Each friend gets 2 whole oranges. 1 orange is left. Cut it into thirds.

Answer: 2 and one third oranges each

Compare shares

More sharers means smaller shares. A pizza for 6 people has smaller pieces than a pizza for 3 people. So one sixth is smaller than one third.

Example

Which is bigger: one fourth or one half of the same sandwich?

2 pieces are bigger than 4 pieces.

Answer: one half

One third is two sixths

Cut each third in half and you get sixths. So one third is the same amount as two sixths.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Calling unequal parts “fourths” or “thirds”The parts must be equal
Thinking one sixth is bigger than one third because 6 is bigger than 3More pieces means smaller pieces, so one sixth is smaller
Thinking two sixths is more than one third because 2 is more than 1They are the same amount
Forgetting the leftover: 5 sandwiches for 2 is “2 each”Cut the leftover too: 2 and a half each
Counting the white parts: 1 of 3 parts shaded is “two thirds”Count the shaded parts: one third
Forgetting to count yourself: “Liam and 2 friends” is 2 peopleCount everyone who shares: 3 people

faq.q: What fractions do Grade 2 students learn in Ontario?
faq.a: In the Ontario math curriculum, Grade 2 students work with halves, thirds, fourths and sixths. They use drawings to share up to 10 items among 2, 3, 4 or 6 people, and they learn that one third is the same as two sixths.

faq.q: What is a fair-share problem in Grade 2 math?
faq.a: A fair-share problem shares items equally, like 5 sandwiches shared by 2 friends. Each friend gets 2 whole sandwiches, and the last one is cut in half, so each gets 2 and a half.

faq.q: Why is one sixth smaller than one third?
faq.a: Share the same pizza with 6 people and with 3 people. With more people each piece is smaller, so one sixth is smaller than one third.

faq.q: Is one third the same as two sixths?
faq.a: Yes. Cut each third of a shape in half and you get sixths, so one third covers the same amount as two sixths. Drawing two bars of the same size is an easy way to show it.

items.q: Which shape is cut into halves?
items.e: Halves are 2 equal parts. That is B. A has 2 parts, but they are not equal. C has 3 equal parts. D has 2 parts, but they are not equal.

items.q: Which shape is cut into thirds?
items.e: Thirds are 3 equal parts. That is C. A has 3 parts, but they are not equal. B has 4 equal parts. D has 2 equal parts.

items.q: Which shape is cut into fourths?
items.e: Fourths are 4 equal parts. That is A. B has 4 parts, but they are not equal. C has 3 equal parts. D has 6 equal parts.

items.q: Which shape is cut into sixths?
items.e: Sixths are 6 equal parts. That is D. A has 4 equal parts. B has 6 parts, but they are not equal. C has 3 equal parts.

items.q: Which shape is not cut into equal parts?
items.e: Look for parts that are different sizes. That is C. A has 6 equal parts. B has 4 equal parts. D has 2 equal parts.

items.q: The shape is cut into equal parts. What are the parts called?
items.e: Count the parts. There are 3 equal parts. 3 equal parts are called thirds.

items.q: The shape is cut into equal parts. What are the parts called?
items.e: Count the parts. There are 6 equal parts. 6 equal parts are called sixths.

items.q: The shape is cut into equal parts. What are the parts called?
items.e: Count the parts. There are 4 equal parts. 4 equal parts are called fourths.

items.q: The shape is cut into equal parts. What are the parts called?
items.e: Count the parts. There are 2 equal parts. 2 equal parts are called halves.

items.q: The shape is cut into equal parts. What are the parts called?
items.e: Count the parts. There are 6 equal parts. 6 equal parts are called sixths.

items.q: What part of the shape is shaded?
items.e: There are 3 equal parts, so they are thirds. 1 part is shaded. So one third is shaded. Do not count the white parts.

items.q: What part of the shape is shaded?
items.e: There are 4 equal parts, so they are fourths. 1 part is shaded. So one fourth is shaded. Do not count the white parts.

items.q: What part of the shape is shaded?
items.e: There are 6 equal parts, so they are sixths. 1 part is shaded. So one sixth is shaded. Do not count the white parts.

items.q: What part of the shape is shaded?
items.e: There are 2 equal parts, so they are halves. 1 part is shaded. So one half is shaded. Do not count the white parts.

items.q: What part of the shape is shaded?
items.e: There are 6 equal parts, so they are sixths. 2 parts are shaded. So two sixths is shaded. Do not count the white parts. (Two sixths is the same as one third.)

items.q: Is the shaded part one fourth of the bar?
c: No. The parts are not equal.
items.e: Fractions need equal parts. These 4 parts are different sizes, so the shaded part is not one fourth.

items.q: Is the shaded part one third of the bar?
c: No. The parts are not equal.
items.e: Fractions need equal parts. All 3 parts are the same size, so the shaded part is one third.

items.q: How many equal parts make thirds?
items.e: 3 equal parts make thirds. Each part is one third.

items.q: How many equal parts make sixths?
items.e: 6 equal parts make sixths. Each part is one sixth.

items.q: How many equal parts make fourths?
items.e: 4 equal parts make fourths. Each part is one fourth.

items.q: 4 cookies are shared equally by 2 friends. How many cookies does each friend get?
items.e: Give out the cookies one at a time to the 2 friends until none are left. Each friend gets 2. Check: 2 + 2 = 4.

items.q: 6 apples are shared equally by 3 friends. How many apples does each friend get?
items.e: Give out the apples one at a time to the 3 friends until none are left. Each friend gets 2. Check: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.
Give out the cookies one at a time to the 4 friends until none are left. Each friend gets 2. Check: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8.

items.q: 10 apples are shared equally by 2 friends. How many apples does each friend get?
items.e: Give out the apples one at a time to the 2 friends until none are left. Each friend gets 5. Check: 5 + 5 = 10.
Give out the cookies one at a time to the 6 friends until none are left. Each friend gets 1. Check: 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 6.
Give out the cookies one at a time to the 3 friends until none are left. Each friend gets 3. Check: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.

items.q: 8 stickers are shared equally by 2 friends. How many stickers does each friend get?
items.e: Give out the stickers one at a time to the 2 friends until none are left. Each friend gets 4. Check: 4 + 4 = 8.

items.q: 3 crackers are shared equally by 3 friends. How many crackers does each friend get?
items.e: Give out the crackers one at a time to the 3 friends until none are left. Each friend gets 1. Check: 1 + 1 + 1 = 3.

items.q: 6 hockey cards are shared equally by 2 friends. How many hockey cards does each friend get?
items.e: Give out the hockey cards one at a time to the 2 friends until none are left. Each friend gets 3. Check: 3 + 3 = 6.

items.q: 4 strawberries are shared equally by 4 friends. How many strawberries does each friend get?
items.e: Give out the strawberries one at a time to the 4 friends until none are left. Each friend gets 1. Check: 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4.

items.q: There are 8 apples. Each friend gets 2. How many friends share the apples?
items.e: Make groups of 2 until all 8 apples are used: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8. That is 4 friends.

items.q: There are 9 muffins. Each friend gets 3. How many friends share the muffins?
items.e: Make groups of 3 until all 9 muffins are used: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9. That is 3 friends.

items.q: There are 6 granola bars. Each friend gets 1. How many friends share the granola bars?
items.e: Make groups of 1 until all 6 granola bars are used: 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 6. That is 6 friends.

items.q: There are 10 crackers. Each friend gets 5. How many friends share the crackers?
items.e: Make groups of 5 until all 10 crackers are used: 5 + 5 = 10. That is 2 friends.

items.q: Which picture shows 8 apples shared fairly by 4 friends?
items.e: Fair means 4 plates with the same number on each: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8. That is C. A has only 2 plates. B has 4 plates, but they are not equal. D has only 3 plates and 6 apples.

items.e: A fair share means every plate has the same number. Two plates have 3 and one plate has 2, so it is not fair.

items.q: 7 cookies are shared equally by 2 friends. Each friend gets 3. How many cookies are left over?
items.e: 2 friends get 3 each: 3 + 3 = 6. 7 − 6 = 1 cookie is left over.

items.q: 10 apples are shared equally by 4 friends. Each friend gets 2. How many apples are left over?
items.e: 4 friends get 2 each: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8. 10 − 8 = 2 apples are left over.

items.q: 9 muffins are shared equally with none left over. How many friends can share them?
items.e: 3 friends get 3 each: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9, none left. With 2, 4 or 6 friends, some muffins are left over.

items.q: 1 pizza is shared equally by 3 friends. The shaded part is one friend’s share. How much pizza does each friend get?
items.e: Cut the pizza into 3 equal pieces (thirds). Each friend gets 1 piece: one third of the pizza.

items.q: 2 sandwiches are shared equally by 3 friends. The shaded part is one friend’s share. How much of a sandwich does each friend get?
items.e: There are fewer sandwiches than friends. Cut each sandwich into thirds. Each friend gets 1 piece from each sandwich. 2 sandwiches, so each friend gets two thirds of a sandwich.

items.q: 3 pizzas are shared equally by 4 friends. The shaded part is one friend’s share. How much pizza does each friend get?
items.e: There are fewer pizzas than friends. Cut each pizza into fourths. Each friend gets 1 piece from each pizza. 3 pizzas, so each friend gets three fourths of a pizza.

items.q: 1 pizza is shared equally by 6 friends. The shaded part is one friend’s share. How much pizza does each friend get?
items.e: Cut the pizza into 6 equal pieces (sixths). Each friend gets 1 piece: one sixth of the pizza.

items.q: 5 pizzas are shared equally by 6 friends. The shaded part is one friend’s share. How much pizza does each friend get?
items.e: There are fewer pizzas than friends. Cut each pizza into sixths. Each friend gets 1 piece from each pizza. 5 pizzas, so each friend gets five sixths of a pizza.

items.q: 1 sandwich is shared equally by 4 friends. The shaded part is one friend’s share. How much of a sandwich does each friend get?
items.e: Cut the sandwich into 4 equal pieces (fourths). Each friend gets 1 piece: one fourth of the sandwich.

items.q: 3 pancakes are shared equally by 2 friends. The shaded parts are one friend’s share. How many pancakes does each friend get?
items.e: Give out whole pancakes first: 1 each, and 1 pancake is left. Cut it into halves. Each friend gets one half more. So each friend gets 1 and a half pancakes.

items.q: 5 sandwiches are shared equally by 2 friends. The shaded parts are one friend’s share. How many sandwiches does each friend get?
items.e: Give out whole sandwiches first: 2 each, and 1 sandwich is left. Cut it into halves. Each friend gets one half more. So each friend gets 2 and a half sandwiches.

items.q: 4 pizzas are shared equally by 3 friends. The shaded parts are one friend’s share. How many pizzas does each friend get?
items.e: Give out whole pizzas first: 1 each, and 1 pizza is left. Cut it into thirds. Each friend gets one third more. So each friend gets 1 and one third pizzas.

items.q: 7 pizzas are shared equally by 4 friends. The shaded parts are one friend’s share. How many pizzas does each friend get?
items.e: Give out whole pizzas first: 1 each, and 3 pizzas are left. Cut each one into fourths. Each friend gets three fourths more. So each friend gets 1 and three fourths pizzas.

items.q: 7 sandwiches are shared equally by 3 friends. The shaded parts are one friend’s share. How many sandwiches does each friend get?
items.e: Give out whole sandwiches first: 2 each, and 1 sandwich is left. Cut it into thirds. Each friend gets one third more. So each friend gets 2 and one third sandwiches.

items.q: 7 pizzas are shared equally by 6 friends. The shaded parts are one friend’s share. How many pizzas does each friend get?
items.e: Give out whole pizzas first: 1 each, and 1 pizza is left. Cut it into sixths. Each friend gets one sixth more. So each friend gets 1 and one sixth pizzas.

items.q: 9 granola bars are shared equally by 2 friends. How many granola bars does each friend get?
items.e: Give out whole granola bars first: 4 each, and 1 granola bar is left. Cut it into halves. Each friend gets one half more. So each friend gets 4 and a half granola bars.

items.q: 10 pancakes are shared equally by 3 friends. How many pancakes does each friend get?
items.e: Give out whole pancakes first: 3 each, and 1 pancake is left. Cut it into thirds. Each friend gets one third more. So each friend gets 3 and one third pancakes.

items.q: 9 muffins are shared equally by 4 friends. How many muffins does each friend get?
items.e: Give out whole muffins first: 2 each, and 1 muffin is left. Cut it into fourths. Each friend gets one fourth more. So each friend gets 2 and one fourth muffins.

items.q: 8 subs are shared equally by 3 friends. How many subs does each friend get?
items.e: Give out whole subs first: 2 each, and 2 subs are left. Cut each one into thirds. Each friend gets two thirds more. So each friend gets 2 and two thirds subs.

items.q: 6 friends share 4 pizzas equally. Does each friend get more or less than 1 pizza?
items.e: Compare the pizzas and the friends. 4 pizzas for 6 friends: there are fewer pizzas than friends, so each friend gets less than 1 pizza (four sixths).

items.q: 4 friends share 5 pizzas equally. Does each friend get more or less than 1 pizza?
items.e: Compare the pizzas and the friends. 5 pizzas for 4 friends: there are more pizzas than friends, so each friend gets 1 pizza and a bit more (1 and one fourth).

items.q: 4 friends share 3 granola bars equally. Each granola bar is cut into fourths. How many fourths does each friend get?
items.e: Each granola bar is cut into 4 equal pieces. Each friend gets 1 piece from each granola bar. There are 3 granola bars, so each friend gets 3 fourths.

items.q: 6 friends share 5 pizzas equally. Each pizza is cut into sixths. How many sixths does each friend get?
items.e: Each pizza is cut into 6 equal pieces. Each friend gets 1 piece from each pizza. There are 5 pizzas, so each friend gets 5 sixths.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which shaded part is bigger?
items.e: The bars are the same size. The top bar has 2 parts and the bottom bar has 4 parts. Fewer parts means bigger parts, so one half is bigger than one fourth.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which shaded part is bigger?
items.e: The bars are the same size. The top bar has 6 parts and the bottom bar has 3 parts. Fewer parts means bigger parts, so one third is bigger than one sixth.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which shaded part is bigger?
items.e: The bars are the same size. The top bar has 4 parts and the bottom bar has 6 parts. Fewer parts means bigger parts, so one fourth is bigger than one sixth.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which shaded part is bigger?
items.e: The bars are the same size. The top bar has 3 parts and the bottom bar has 2 parts. Fewer parts means bigger parts, so one half is bigger than one third.

items.q: Same size pizzas. Which piece is bigger: one sixth or one fourth?
items.e: Think of the same pizza. Cut into 4 pieces, the pieces are bigger than cut into 6 pieces. So one fourth is bigger than one sixth.

items.q: Same size pizzas. Which piece is bigger: one half or one third?
items.e: Think of the same pizza. Cut into 2 pieces, the pieces are bigger than cut into 3 pieces. So one half is bigger than one third.

items.q: Same size pizzas. Which piece is smaller: one third or one sixth?
items.e: Think of the same pizza. Cut into 3 pieces, the pieces are bigger than cut into 6 pieces. So one sixth is smaller than one third.

items.q: Same size pizzas. Which piece is smaller: one fourth or one half?
items.e: Think of the same pizza. Cut into 2 pieces, the pieces are bigger than cut into 4 pieces. So one fourth is smaller than one half.

items.q: Same size pizzas. Which piece is smaller: one sixth or one half?
items.e: Think of the same pizza. Cut into 2 pieces, the pieces are bigger than cut into 6 pieces. So one sixth is smaller than one half.

items.q: Zoe’s group of 2 shares a pizza equally. Liam’s group of 6 shares the same size pizza. Whose group gets bigger pieces?
items.e: The same size pizza cut for 2 people has bigger pieces than one cut for 6 people. One half is bigger than one sixth, so Zoe’s group gets bigger pieces.

items.q: Maya’s group of 4 shares a pan of brownies equally. Owen’s group of 3 shares the same size pan of brownies. Whose group gets bigger pieces?
items.e: The same size pan of brownies cut for 3 people has bigger pieces than one cut for 4 people. One third is bigger than one fourth, so Owen’s group gets bigger pieces.

items.q: Priya’s group of 6 shares a cake equally. Noah’s group of 4 shares the same size cake. Whose group gets bigger pieces?
items.e: The same size cake cut for 4 people has bigger pieces than one cut for 6 people. One fourth is bigger than one sixth, so Noah’s group gets bigger pieces.

items.q: 6 cookies can be shared equally by 2 friends or by 3 friends. When does each friend get more?
items.e: Fewer friends means a bigger share for each friend. 6 cookies shared by 2 gives each friend 3. Shared by 3, each friend gets 2.

items.q: A pizza can be shared equally by 4 friends or by 6 friends. When does each friend get more?
items.e: Fewer friends means a bigger share for each friend. A pizza shared by 4 gives each friend one fourth. Shared by 6, each friend gets one sixth.

items.q: 4 sandwiches can be shared equally by 4 friends or by 2 friends. When does each friend get more?
items.e: Fewer friends means a bigger share for each friend. 4 sandwiches shared by 2 gives each friend 2. Shared by 4, each friend gets 1.

items.q: Which piece is the biggest? All the pizzas are the same size.
items.e: A pizza cut into 2 pieces has the biggest pieces. One half is the biggest.

items.q: Which piece is the smallest? All the pizzas are the same size.
items.e: A pizza cut into 6 pieces has the smallest pieces. One sixth is the smallest.

items.q: Kai says one sixth of a pizza is bigger than one third of the same pizza, because 6 is more than 3. Is he right?
items.e: 6 people share the pizza for sixths, and 3 people share it for thirds. More sharers means smaller pieces. So one third is bigger than one sixth.

items.q: Amira says one fourth of a sandwich is bigger than one half of the same sandwich. Is she right?
items.e: Cut a sandwich into 2 pieces or into 4 pieces. The 2 pieces are bigger. So one half is bigger than one fourth.

items.q: Put the pieces in order from biggest to smallest: one sixth, one half, one third
c: one third, one half, one sixth
one half, one third, one sixth
one sixth, one third, one half
one half, one sixth, one third
items.e: Fewer pieces means bigger pieces. Halves (2 pieces) are biggest, then thirds (3), then sixths (6): one half, one third, one sixth.

sets.title: One third is two sixths: word problems

items.q: The bars are the same size. Is the shaded amount the same?
items.e: Cut each third in half and you get sixths. One third covers the same space as two sixths.

items.q: The top bar shows one third. How many sixths cover the same amount?
items.e: Each third is 2 sixths. So one third is the same as two sixths.

items.q: Which bar shows the same amount as one third?
items.e: One third is the same as two sixths. That is A. B shows one sixth. C shows three sixths. D shows two fourths.

items.q: The bars are the same size. The top bar shows one half. What does the bottom bar show?
items.e: The bottom bar has 4 equal parts and 2 are shaded: two fourths. It is the same as one half.

items.q: One third of a pizza is the same as how many sixths?
items.e: Cut each third into 2 equal pieces. One third becomes two sixths.

items.q: Which is the same amount as two sixths?
items.e: Two sixths fill the same space as one third. Two thirds would be 4 sixths.

items.q: Owen eats one third of a sub. Ava eats two sixths of the same size sub. Who eats more?
items.e: Two sixths is the same as one third. So they eat the same amount.

items.q: Zoe says two sixths of a pie is more than one third of the same pie, because 2 is more than 1. Is she right?
items.e: Sixths are smaller pieces. Two sixths fill the same space as one third, so they are the same.

items.q: A pan of brownies is cut into 6 equal pieces. 3 friends share it fairly. How many pieces does each friend get?
items.e: 6 pieces for 3 friends: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6. Each friend gets 2 pieces. That is two sixths, the same as one third.

items.q: Kai cuts a sub into thirds and eats 1 piece. Hana cuts the same size sub into sixths. How many pieces must Hana eat to eat the same amount as Kai?
items.e: One third is the same as two sixths. Hana must eat 2 pieces.

items.q: On a canoe trip, 2 friends share 5 granola bars equally. How many granola bars does each friend get?
items.e: Give out whole bars: 2 each, and 1 bar is left. Cut it in half. Each friend gets 2 and a half granola bars.

items.q: At recess, 3 friends share 7 oranges equally. How many oranges does each friend get?
items.e: Give out whole oranges: 2 each, and 1 is left. Cut it into thirds. Each friend gets 2 and one third oranges.

items.q: After hockey practice, 6 players share 4 oranges equally. How much orange does each player get?
items.e: Cut each orange into sixths. Each player gets 1 piece from each of the 4 oranges: four sixths of an orange.

items.q: On a snow day, 4 friends share 3 muffins equally. How much muffin does each friend get?
items.e: Cut each muffin into fourths. Each friend gets 1 piece from each of the 3 muffins: three fourths of a muffin.

items.q: At a March Break sleepover, 4 friends share 10 pancakes equally. How many pancakes does each friend get?
items.e: Give out whole pancakes: 2 each, and 2 are left. Cut each into fourths. Each friend gets 2 more fourths. So each friend gets 2 and two fourths pancakes (the same as 2 and a half).

items.q: Ethan and Priya share 7 maple cookies equally. How many cookies does each child get?
items.e: Give out whole cookies: 3 each, and 1 is left. Cut it in half. Each child gets 3 and a half cookies.

items.q: Liam and 2 friends share 9 hockey cards equally. How many cards does each person get?
items.e: Liam and 2 friends are 3 people. 3 + 3 + 3 = 9, so each person gets 3 cards.

items.q: At lunch, Emma’s group of 3 shares a pizza. Noah’s group of 6 shares the same size pizza. Whose group gets bigger pieces?
items.e: Fewer people means bigger pieces. One third is bigger than one sixth, so Emma’s group gets bigger pieces. Each piece for Emma’s group is as big as 2 pieces for Noah’s group.

items.q: Arjun cuts a pizza into 6 pieces. The pieces are different sizes. He says each piece is one sixth. Is he right?
c: No. Each piece is one third.

items.e: Sixths must be 6 equal parts. The pieces are different sizes, so they are not sixths.

items.q: At Thanksgiving, 6 cousins share 9 pumpkin tarts equally. How many tarts does each cousin get?
items.e: Give out whole tarts: 1 each, and 3 are left. Cut each into sixths. Each cousin gets 3 more sixths. So each cousin gets 1 and three sixths tarts (the same as 1 and a half).
